These include theoretical DEB rules (snippets 4,5,12,14,15,18) and empirical observations (2,8,11). A smaller subset reports opposite trends, notably in Daphnia studies where higher food leads to smaller eggs (1,3,17), but these are outweighed by the numerous supportive references across taxa and theoretical frameworks. Neutral passages discuss related topics without addressing the nutrition‑egg size link directly. Consequently, the corpus offers strong overall evidence favoring the covariation of egg size with maternal nutritional status.

snippets.text: Three experiments were conducted to investigate the influence of diet composition and body weight on early egg size. Increasing dietary protein or methionine level had little or no effect on egg size for the first 12 weeks of production.
